Content: `text(Two)` populations of a species of squirrel are geographically isolated from each other. Although they have the same population density, `text(one)` population is significantly larger in number than the other. A new bacterial disease, which is easily spread and extremely virulent, affects both populations at the same time.
Which of the following is the best prediction of how the new disease will affect the `text(two)` populations?

A.Choice: The `text(two)` populations will be equally affected, because the ability to trigger an immune response is randomly distributed among all squirrels of that species.

B.Choice: The larger population will be less affected by the disease than will the smaller population, because the mutation rate of the larger population is higher than the mutation rate of the smaller population.

C.Choice: The smaller population will be more affected than will the larger population, because the smaller population has less genetic variation than the larger population has.

D.Choice: The smaller population will be less affected than will the larger population, because the smaller population exhibits more genetic drift than the larger population exhibits.

Content: Mitochondria are found in most eukaryotic cells and contain their own `text(DNA)` and ribosomes that are similar to those typical of many prokaryotic cells. Which of the following statements is justified by these observations?

A.Choice: The mitochondrion is the only location in which eukaryotic cells can synthesize `text(ATP)`.

B.Choice: An ancestral cell most likely engulfed an aerobic prokaryote in a relationship that proved beneficial for both cells.

C.Choice: Mitochondrial membranes provide abundant surface area for reactions because of the infoldings called cristae.

D.Choice: The mitochondrion plays a role in respiration, but it also stores the cell's extra `text(mRNA)`.

Content: Sickle-cell anemia is associated with a mutation in the gene encoding the beta subunit of hemoglobin that results in a change from glutamic acid to valine at position `6`. All other amino acids are identical to a normal hemoglobin molecule.
Based on the information above, which of the following mutations is the most likely cause of sickle-cell anemia?

A.Choice: A `text(single)` base-pair substitution in the gene encoding the beta subunit

B.Choice: A `text(single)` base-pair insertion in the gene encoding the beta subunit

C.Choice: A `text(single)` base-pair deletion in the gene encoding the beta subunit

D.Choice: A translocation of `text(DNA)` from `text(one)` chromosome to another

Content: In the `text(year 2000)`, specimens of Caulerpa taxifolia, a green alga used in tropical aquariums, were found off the coast of California. Native to the Indian Ocean, C. taxifolia is known for aggressive growth and an ability to compete with sea grasses. It is currently on an international list of invasive species. Which of the following best predicts the consequences of the introduction of C. taxifolia to the California coast?

A.Choice: Without natural herbivores or competitors, C. taxifolia will grow rapidly and crowd out native species of producers.

B.Choice: C. taxifolia will have a hard time establishing itself because it will have to compete against native species of sea grasses, which are better adapted to the environment.

C.Choice: C. taxifolia will grow rapidly, leading to an increase in the diversity of producers.

D.Choice: Because it is not in the Indian Ocean, its natural environment, C. taxifolia will not be able to grow efficiently.

Content: Which of the following statements is best supported by the data?

A.Choice: Black bears are a keystone species.

B.Choice: Salmon are a keystone species.

C.Choice: Black bear urine is a significant source of nitrogen in the environment.

D.Choice: The presence of black bears and salmon correlates with a significant increase in nitrogen influx.

Content: Which of the following most likely describes how the interaction between bears and salmon influences nitrogen dynamics in the environment?

A.Choice: When bears consume salmon, they leave parts of the carcasses on the ground, which decompose, releasing nitrogen into the environment.

B.Choice: When salmon swim upstream to spawn, bears migrate to the rivers and deposit nitrogen from the forest with their excrement.

C.Choice: Bears are a reservoir for nitrogen because they are the top consumer in the environment.

D.Choice: Bears urinate in rivers and streams, which provides nitrogen for the salmon.

Content: Which of the following pieces of additional data would help further investigate the relationship between bears, salmon, and influx of nitrogen into the local environment?

A.Choice: The experimenters should remove the remains of salmon carcasses immediately after the salmon are eaten by the bears and determine the nitrogen content of the carcasses.

B.Choice: The experimenters should increase the number of bears in the area and measure the amount of nitrogen available for uptake by plants.

C.Choice: The experimenters should set up a net to catch salmon before they enter the area and then measure nitrogen influx.

D.Choice: The experimenters should clear-cut the trees from the area and determine how much nitrogen remains in the streams.

Content: If a dam is built downstream and prevents salmon migration to the test sites, which of the following most accurately predicts the impact on nitrogen influx?

A.Choice: Nitrogen influx will increase because the bears will no longer store nitrogen from the salmon.

B.Choice: Nitrogen influx will decrease because there will be less bear-salmon interaction.

C.Choice: Nitrogen influx will remain stable because organisms other than bears and salmon will mobilize nitrogen in the environment.

D.Choice: Nitrogen influx will increase because bears will no longer lose nitrogen to the salmon.

Content: Eye pigment in a particular strain of fly is determined by `text(two)` genes. An autosomal gene that controls the color of the pigments in the eye has `text(two)` alleles: a dominant allele (`R`) that results in red eyes and a recessive allele (`r`) that results in sepia eyes. A sex-linked gene that controls the expression of the colored pigments also has `text(two)` alleles: a dominant allele (`T`) that allows for expression of the colored pigments and a recessive allele (`t`) that does not allow for expression of the colored pigments. Individuals without a `T` allele have white eyes regardless of the alleles of other eye-color genes.
Which of the following represents a cross between a white-eyed female and a red-eyed male?

B.Choice: `TtX^rX^rxxt tX^RY`

C.Choice: `R RX^TX^TxxRrX^TY`

D.Choice: `RrX^tX^txxRrX^TY`

Content: Some strains of the bacterium Streptococcus pyogenes secrete poisonous substances called exotoxins. The genes encoding the exotoxins are thought to have originated in bacteriophages, which are viruses that infect bacteria.
Which of the following is the most likely mechanism by which the S. pyogenes acquired the ability to produce the exotoxins?

A.Choice: Bacteriophages engulfed cellular debris from dead bacteria.

B.Choice: Bacteriophages in the environment activated bacterial cell division.

C.Choice: Bacteriophage `text(DNA)` became integrated in the bacterial chromosome.

D.Choice: Bacteriophage proteins were absorbed into bacteria cells by endocytosis.

Content: Using the model of speciation and applying it to a different population, which of the following outcomes is most consistent for a different species in which the males are homogametic and the females are heterogametic?

A.Choice: Sterility would appear in females before appearing in males.

B.Choice: Speciation would occur more rapidly because females would produce more offspring.

C.Choice: Behavioral isolation would occur sooner in species exhibiting nonrandom mating.

D.Choice: The population would reach Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium at an accelerated rate.

Content: A scientist is evaluating a proposal for raising large numbers of fish in ocean pens for human consumption. As part of the evaluation, the scientist is designing a plan for investigating how the fish in the ocean pens might affect nearby ecosystems.

Content: Epinephrine is a protein hormone found in many animals. Epinephrine stimulates a signaling pathway that results in the breakdown of glycogen to glucose in the liver cells. Which of the following describes the initial steps in the process whereby epinephrine stimulates glycogen breakdown?

A.Choice: Epinephrine binds to a cell-surface receptor; the activated receptor stimulates production of the `text(second)` messenger, `text(cAMP)`.

B.Choice: Epinephrine binds to a cell-surface receptor; the activated receptor catalyzes the conversion of glycogen to glucose.

C.Choice: Epinephrine diffuses through the plasma membrane; the hormone dimerizes in the cytosol.

D.Choice: Epinephrine is taken into the cell by endocytosis; glycogen is converted to glucose in the endocytotic vesicle.

Content: A group of students designed an experiment to determine the effect of compost on the germination and growth of plants. The students set up experimental plots by mixing different ratios of soil and compost. They planted `20` pea and `20` melon seeds in `text(each plot)` and watered `text(each plot)` regularly. The students recorded the number of seeds that germinated, and as the plants grew, they recorded plant length, number and size of leaves, and general health observations.
The following observations were recorded.

:ibox:• In all treatments, more pea seeds germinated than melon seeds.
• There was a `text(week)` of rainy weather at `text(three weeks)`.
• Melon plants developed a fungal growth at `text(four weeks)`.
• Melon plants grew longer than pea plants, but many melon leaves showed signs of yellowing as the `text(weeks)` passed.
The students concluded that pea plants grew better in compost than did melon plants.
Which of the following best addresses the validity of the conclusion made by the students?

A.Choice: The conclusion is valid because the independent and dependent variables in the experiment were controlled.

B.Choice: The conclusion is valid because the experimental design included a large sample size.

C.Choice: The conclusion is invalid because other variables in the experiment (both biotic and abiotic) affected the results.

D.Choice: The conclusion is invalid because the units of measurement were not given in the experimental design.

Content: Butterflies of the genus Colias live in the Rocky Mountains, where they experience a wide range of temperatures. Different variants of a particular glycolytic enzyme in the flight muscles are optimally active at different temperatures. Within the same population, some individual butterflies fly most effectively at `29°text(C)`, while others fly most effectively at `40°text(C)`. Still others can be equally active at both temperatures.
Which of the following claims is most consistent with the observed butterfly behavior?

A.Choice: Butterflies that express `text(two)` variants of the enzyme are active over a greater range of temperature.

B.Choice: Butterflies that are active over a wide range of temperatures produce greater amounts of the enzyme.

C.Choice: Temperature has little effect on the activity of butterflies.

D.Choice: Butterflies that are active at warmer temperatures produce more offspring.

Content: High blood cholesterol (hypercholesterolemia, `text(HC)`) can lead to cardiovascular problems such as atherosclerosis and heart attack. Exercise and monitoring of diet can often control cholesterol levels; however, in certain cases `text(HC)` is inherited as an autosomal dominant disease caused by a mutation in a `text(single)` gene.

A.Choice: How important are the results of the test to the couple's health, since they already know they have `text(HC)`?

B.Choice: How can they eliminate the allele for `text(HC)` from their cells?

C.Choice: If both have the allele for `text(HC)`, should an insurance company raise their rates because of the results of the test?

D.Choice: What cures are available for `text(HC)` other than dietary changes and exercise?

The yellow-fever mosquito (Aedes aegypti) is a major vector of human disease. In a particular location in Africa, there are `text(two)` forms of the mosquito. The forest form of the mosquito is black and often lays its eggs in tree holes and pools of water in the forest. The domestic form of the mosquito is brown and prefers to lay its eggs in rainwater collected near human dwellings.

Researchers used a choice chamber (Figure `1`) to investigate the host preference of A. aegypti. The researchers recorded the number of forest-form and domestic-form mosquitoes that bit human or guinea pig hosts during several `text(ten-minute)` trials. The researchers used these data to calculate a host-preference index for `text(each form)`, as shown in Figure `2`. Researchers also identified a gene in the mosquitoes, `text(OR4)`, that encodes an olfactory receptor. A volatile odorant, sulcatone, binds to the `text(OR4)` receptor. Humans produce higher levels of sulcatone than do guinea pigs.
Based on an analysis of the data, `ultext(identify)` the preferred host of the forest form `ultext(and)` of the domestic form of the mosquito.
